  "scenario": "A vendor's closed-source tax-and-fee calculator binary (feecalc) is installed on the system. The company's procurement team has been told to replace it with an open Python implementation before the vendor contract expires. No source code, no documentation—only the binary and a folder of sample orders. An engineer must systematically probe the binary to discover every rule (tax rates, exemptions, discount tiers, coupon logic, fee caps, rounding mode, error messages), then build a Python program that produces byte-identical output for any order of the same kinds.",
  "environment_setup": "A multi-stage Dockerfile builds a C reference program (environment/reference.c, ~280 lines, stdlib only) with gcc -O2, strips it, and installs the binary at /usr/local/bin/feecalc. The final image (ubuntu:24.04) has python3 and gcc installed. A sample file /app/sample.txt contains ~28 example orders separated by lines containing only ===, covering every input kind: all 10 states (CA, TX, NY, FL, WA, OR, MA, IL, PA, OH), all 3 customer types, tax_exempt flag, all 4 item categories (general, food, clothing, medicine), quantities at discount boundaries (9, 10, 49, 50, 100), subtotals at bulk boundaries (~$25, ~$500, ~$1000), all 5 coupon codes plus invalid and missing, all 3 shipping methods, all 5 zones, all 5 payment methods, and all 7 error cases (unknown state, negative quantity, negative price, unknown payment, unknown shipping method, invalid zone, no items, missing field). The reference source is never in the final image. The binary uses integer cents internally with round-half-away-from-zero arithmetic, making rounding behavior deterministic and distinguishable from Python's default banker's rounding.",
  "instruction_summary": "Create /app/quotelib.py that reads the same text-based order format as feecalc from stdin (key=value lines for STATE, TYPE, TAX_EXEMPT, PAYMENT, SHIP_METHOD, SHIP_ZONE, COUPON; 'ITEM <category> <quantity> <unit_price>' lines for items) and writes 12 key=value output lines (SUBTOTAL, QTY_DISCOUNT, BULK_DISCOUNT, COUPON_DISCOUNT, TAXABLE, TAX, SHIPPING, FUEL, HANDLING, SMALL_ORDER_FEE, PAYMENT_SURCHARGE, TOTAL) with amounts formatted to exactly 2 decimal places. On validation error, write 'ERROR: ...' to stderr and exit 1 with no stdout. On success exit 0. The program must produce exactly the same stdout, stderr, and exit status as /usr/local/bin/feecalc for any input of the kinds in /app/sample.txt. It must not call feecalc or any external program. The binary will be unavailable when checked. The program should also be importable as a module (from quotelib import calculate where calculate(text:str)->str raises ValueError on invalid input). The agent is told to probe the binary systematically and that /app/sample.txt contains multiple orders separated by === lines, each block fed individually to feecalc.",
  "solution_outline": [
    "Write /app/quotelib.py implementing the full calculation pipeline in Python using integer cents and a round-half-away-from-zero helper (matching C's round() for positive and negative values).",
    "Parse input lines: STATE=, TYPE=, TAX_EXEMPT=, PAYMENT=, SHIP_METHOD=, SHIP_ZONE=, COUPON=, ITEM lines. Ignore blank and unknown lines.",
    "Validate in order: missing STATE, missing TYPE, missing PAYMENT, missing SHIP_METHOD, missing SHIP_ZONE, no items, unknown state, unknown type, unknown payment, unknown shipping method, invalid zone (not 1-5), negative quantity (first offending item), negative price (first offending item). Each error writes exact message to stderr and exits 1.",
    "Compute per-item: ext_cents = quantity * price_cents. Quantity discount: >=50 → 10%, >=10 → 5%, else 0, rounded half-up per line.",
    "Subtotal = sum of ext_cents. Bulk discount: subtotal >= $1000 → 5%, >= $500 → 3%, applied after quantity discounts, rounded half-up.",
    "Coupon: look up code in internal table. SAVE10 (10% percent, no min), SAVE20 (20% percent, min $100 post-discount), DOLLAR5 ($5 fixed, min $50 post-discount), DOLLAR25 ($25 fixed, min $200 post-discount), FREESHIP (zeroes shipping). Invalid code = no discount, not an error. Minimum checked against subtotal after qty+bulk discounts.",
    "Exempt amount: sum of (ext - qty_disc) for food items in CA/NY/MA/PA, clothing items in PA, medicine items in all states. Uses post-qty-discount extension.",
    "Taxable = discounted_subtotal - exempt_amount + shipping (only in TX/FL/OH). If government type or tax_exempt=true: TAX=0, TAXABLE=0. Otherwise tax = round_half_up(taxable * rate_bp / 10000).",
    "State rates in basis points: CA 725, TX 625, NY 800, FL 600, WA 650, OR 0, MA 625, IL 625, PA 600, OH 575.",
    "Shipping table: standard [5.00, 8.50, 12.00, 15.50, 20.00], express [10.00, 15.00, 20.00, 25.00, 32.00], overnight [20.00, 28.00, 38.00, 48.00, 60.00] by zone 1-5.",
    "Fuel = 10% of shipping rounded half-up, capped at $5.00. Handling = $2.00 + $0.50 * total_quantity, capped at $10.00. Small order fee = $5.00 if pre-discount subtotal < $25.00.",
    "Payment surcharge rates: credit_card 2.5%, debit 0%, ach -0.5%, cash 0%, gift_card 1%. Applied to (discounted_subtotal + tax + shipping + fuel + handling + small_order_fee), rounded half-up.",
    "Total = total_before + payment_surcharge. Output all 12 fields with %.2f formatting. Also provide importable calculate(text)->str that raises ValueError with the error message on invalid input."

    "test_artifact_exists: Assert /app/quotelib.py exists and is a valid Python file.",

    "test_sample_inputs: Read /app/sample.txt, split on === lines, feed each non-empty block to both programs, compare stdout+stderr+exit code.",

    "test_coupon_logic: SAVE10 (always applies), SAVE20 (min $100 post-discount), DOLLAR5 (min $50), DOLLAR25 (min $200), FREESHIP (zeroes shipping+fuel), invalid code (no discount, exit 0). Test minimum boundary with discounted subtotals.",
    "test_fee_caps: Overnight zone 5 (shipping $60 → fuel capped at $5.00); 17 items (handling $10.50 → capped at $10.00); 16 items (handling $10.00, not capped).",

Compare exact stderr and exit code. Test validation order (first error wins)."

  "anti_cheat": "The reference C source is only in the builder stage of the Dockerfile and in tests/reference.c; it is never in the final image the agent sees. The binary is stripped (no symbol table, no debug info). Tests rename /usr/local/bin/feecalc before running the artifact, so the artifact cannot shell out to it. The compiled reference binary used by tests is at a non-obvious temp path the artifact cannot discover. The generated test inputs use a fixed seed in gen_cases.py which is in tests/ (never visible to the agent), so the artifact cannot hard-code expected outputs. The 500 generated inputs include boundary values and rounding ties that only a correct implementation handles. Any solution that outputs nothing, deletes files, or hard-codes the sample outputs fails on the generated cases. The agent must implement the full calculation pipeline to pass.",
  "failure_modes": "A capable agent is likely to fail in these ways, all due to insufficient probing: (1) Using Python's built-in round() which uses banker's rounding (half-even) instead of half-up; fails on tie cases like CA $2.00 taxable where tax should be $0.15 not $0.14. (2) Assuming TAXABLE shows the taxable base even for exempt customers; fails because the binary outputs TAXABLE=0.00 for government/tax_exempt. (3) Not discovering that TX/FL/OH add shipping to the taxable amount; fails on those states. (4) Guessing the wrong set of food-exempt states; fails when tested on a state the agent didn't probe. (5) Applying bulk discount before quantity discount or coupon before bulk; fails on orders with multiple discount types. (6) Missing the fuel or handling caps; fails on high-value orders. (7) Checking coupon minimums against pre-discount subtotal instead of post-discount; fails on boundary cases. (8) Forgetting that FREESHIP zeroes fuel as well as shipping. (9) Not implementing ACH as a negative surcharge. (10) Getting error messages or validation order wrong; fails on error-case tests. Each failure stems from not running enough probing inputs to discover a rule that is observable but not obvious.",
  "challenge_kind": "executable_reference",

On success: writes 12 lines to stdout (SUBTOTAL, QTY_DISCOUNT, BULK_DISCOUNT, COUPON_DISCOUNT, TAXABLE, TAX, SHIPPING, FUEL, HANDLING, SMALL_ORDER_FEE, PAYMENT_SURCHARGE, TOTAL) each as KEY=<amount> with 2 decimal places, exits 0. On error: writes 'ERROR: <message>' to stderr, nothing to stdout, exits 1. The Python artifact at /app/quotelib.py is invoked as 'python3 /app/quotelib.py' with the same stdin/stdout/stderr/exit-code contract.",

  "shortcut_guard": "Tests compile a fresh reference binary from tests/reference.c (pristine source never in the image), rename /usr/local/bin/feecalc to feecalc.hidden before running the artifact so it cannot be called, and place the compiled reference at a non-obvious temp path. The 500 generated inputs use a fixed seed in gen_cases.py (in tests/, invisible to the agent) and include boundary and rounding-tie cases that only a correct full implementation passes. The artifact cannot hard-code outputs because it does not know which inputs will be tested. An artifact that outputs nothing or deletes files fails immediately. An artifact that tries to call the original binary gets 'file not found'. An artifact that tries strings/decompilation on the binary gets nothing useful (binary is stripped and hidden) and cannot discover numeric tables (rates, thresholds, caps) from strings alone."
